title: Dispensing by administration of influenza vaccine, COVID-19 vaccine and Department-designated immunizations under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(6)
rule_summary: 105 CMR 700.004(B), headed Exemptions from Requirement to Register, provides at paragraph (6) that a registered pharmacist, pharmacy intern, and pharmacy technician may dispense by administration influenza vaccine, COVID-19 vaccine, and other immunizations designated by the Department to persons five years of age or older provided that: (a) such registered pharmacist, pharmacy intern, or pharmacy technician is authorized to dispense controlled substances in accordance with M.G.L. c. 112 or Department guidance; (b) such administration is conducted pursuant to the order of a practitioner; (c) each pharmacy that provides immunizations shall follow Department guidelines to disclose whether it receives vaccines free of charge through the Massachusetts Immunization Program and shall notify patients that there may be a difference in cost between immunization services provided at a pharmacy and at a primary care provider's office; and (d) such activity is conducted in accordance with guidelines adopted by the Department which shall include, but not be limited to, requirements for: 1. training accredited by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the American Council on Pharmaceutical Education or a similar health authority or professional body; 2. pre-administration education and screening; 3. vaccine storage and handling; 4. administration of medication, including administration of controlled substances as necessary for the management of medical emergencies; 5. where immunization is being administered to a person younger than 18 years old, providing information on primary care providers in the pharmacy's geographic area; 6. if the purpose of the visit is for a childhood immunization other than the influenza vaccine, providing counseling on the importance of establishing and maintaining a relationship with a pediatric or family practice for ongoing medical and well-child care; 7. record keeping; and 8. reporting of adverse events.
exam_relevance: Tests who the paragraph names, which immunizations it reaches, the age floor of five years, the practitioner's order as the instrument, the pharmacy's disclosure and cost notice, and the subjects the Department's guidelines must address, and keeps this immunization authority apart from dispensing by administration under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) and from vaccine administration under a Commissioner's order under 105 CMR 700.003(F).

authority.name: Massachusetts Department of Public Health regulations
authority.section: 105 CMR 700.004(B)(6), read with the heading of 105 CMR 700.004(B)

numeric_facts.fact: minimum age of a person to whom immunizations may be dispensed by administration under the paragraph
numeric_facts.conditions: influenza vaccine, COVID-19 vaccine and other immunizations designated by the Department, pursuant to the order of a practitioner

numeric_facts.fact: age below which the Department's guidelines must require information on primary care providers in the pharmacy's geographic area
numeric_facts.conditions: where immunization is being administered to a person younger than 18 years old

common_confusions: Applying the 18-or-older age limit of 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) to immunizations under paragraph (6), which reaches persons five years of age or older.
Treating the eligible-medication list issued as Department guidance under 105 CMR 700.004(B)(9) as governing the immunizations that paragraph (6) separately authorizes.
Overlooking that the instrument under paragraph (6) is the order of a practitioner.
Overlooking the pharmacy's disclosure of whether it receives vaccines free of charge through the Massachusetts Immunization Program and its notice to patients of a possible difference in cost.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the current text of 105 CMR 700.000 published by the Department of Public Health on mass.gov (the 39-page edition whose PDF was generated on 2024-02-02), including the heading of 105 CMR 700.004(B) and paragraph (6)(a) through (d).
